title: Nobbs (Goose Creek)
summary: Nobbs is a Flanders-area placename associated with Goose Creek, one of the creeks named in Paucamp's testimony about the west end of Peconic Bay.
introduction_content: Nobbs is connected with the creek now known as Goose Creek near Flanders, flowing into the Great Peconic Bay. The name belongs to a chain of Peconic Bay creek names preserved through testimony by Paucamp, a Corchaug sachem.
history_content: The placename brings together the creek location, fishing-station context, and related Peconic Bay place-name sequence. The overview stays broad while dated source details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
No separate alternate spelling is listed for Nobbs. The name may be a shortened form of a longer word connected with white-fish or bony-fish, associated with fish used as fertilizer for planting.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are a vital part of living on the land, for they both describe the land as well as function as trail markers and guides to the land.”

— Aliana Violet Parker, Learning the Language of the Land (2012), PDF page 30, Place Names discussion, opening sentence
whereintheworld_content: Approximate general point at the modern Goose Creek feature near Flanders. The map placement is for orientation only, not an exact historic fishing-station coordinate.
